findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any file-not-found or I/O error
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>, use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e))

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) emits logging inside the parsing/iteration logic
findings.failure_mode: pure parsing code has a side effect that corrupts stdout, breaks piped consumers, and violates Data/Calculations/Actions separation; logging in the shell is indistinguishable from core logic
findings.fix: remove println! entirely from load_metrics; metrics/logging belongs only in the imperative shell layer, never in data construction

findings.problem: parts[0] indexes into a Vec<String> with no bounds check
findings.failure_mode: a malformed line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields triggers an index-out-of-bounds panic at runtime
findings.fix: use parts.get(0).ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) or parse with split_once and map_err

findings.problem: parts[1] indexes into a Vec<String> with no bounds check
findings.failure_mode: a line with exactly one field (no comma) panics on parts[1]
findings.fix: use parts.get(1) with ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) or split_once to avoid double allocation

findings.failure_mode: any non-numeric value in the second field (e.g., "abc") aborts the process instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid) and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.problem: (...).parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 performs a lossy cast from u32 to u16
findings.failure_mode: values in the range 65536..=4294967295 silently wrap to u16 range, corrupting data without any error or warning; a value of 70000 becomes 14464
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) to catch out-of-range values

findings.problem: load_metrics fuses file I/O, println! logging, unbounded Vec allocation, string splitting, parsing, and domain construction into a single pub function
findings.failure_mode: violates Data/Calculations/Actions architecture; the shell cannot be tested independently from I/O; pure logic is polluted with side effects; no allocation cap exists; the function owns both transport and domain concerns
findings.fix: split into: 1) shell fn load_metrics(path) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> that calls a pure parse_records(text) helper; 2) remove println!; 3) use split_once and try_reserve with a domain cap; 4) return Result with typed errors throughout

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(|p| p.trim().to_string()).collect() allocates a Vec<String> for every line instead of using split_once
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary intermediate allocation on every line; split_once is mandatory per SKILL.md for one-separator grammars; the collect()-based approach allocates N strings then discards all but two
findings.fix: let (_name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)?; then parse value_str.trim() directly

findings.problem: Record uses raw String for name and u16 for value with no validation invariants
findings.failure_mode: any caller can construct Record with empty names, negative-looking values via overflow, or otherwise invalid state; the domain has no enforcement of value semantics
findings.fix: add a smart constructor or parse function that validates name is non-empty and value is in range; consider making fields private and exposing only validated access

findings.problem: No try_reserve or domain-cap check before collecting into Vec<Record>; input lines are unbounded
findings.failure_mode: a very large file causes unbounded heap allocation with no cap, no graceful OOM handling, and no allocation-failure typed error
findings.fix: after validating any max_items cap, call values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation)?; enforce a domain maximum on line count

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence for load_metrics; allocates a Vec per line then collects into a Vec<Record>
findings.failure_mode: cannot verify whether the allocation pattern is acceptable for the target workload; no baseline to compare against; performance claims are unverifiable
findings.fix: add a criterion or similar benchmark measuring throughput and allocations for realistic input sizes; add allocation analysis via cargo-flamegraph or similar
